description: List the notebooks open in the runtime, with each one's run state. `this_session` marks this session's notebook; if none has it, the session has no notebook yet and `new_notebook` makes one. `pending_run` is the edited cells not yet run, `running` the cells queued or running, `packages` the package install under way if there is one, and `execution_allowed` is false in safe preview or while the notebook's process is stopped. A session changes only its own notebook. If the user asks you to work in one whose `this_session` is false: when this session has no notebook yet, `open_notebook` with its path joins it; otherwise tell the user that needs a new session.
name: list_notebooks

description: Read one cell: its code, its output, and whether it is `running`, `queued`, `errored`, `code_folded` or `stale` (edited and not yet run; in an R notebook also a result made before a cell it depends on last ran). An R notebook's cell that hasn't run since the notebook opened or restarted has `not_run`. Counts as the read an edit needs. If the code is what this session read or wrote in its last few calls, it is left out and `code_unchanged` is true; pass `include_code=true` to get it anyway. For rich values (tables, arrays, HTML), `output` only names the type and `output_text` has the value as text, cut at 16 KB. An errored cell has an `error` object with its `kind` and, when known, a `hint`. A read of a cell that a run you started is running or will run waits up to 45 seconds for it to finish, so read it again only if it is still `running`; its `message` then says how long it waited. While packages install, a queued cell's read waits up to 45 seconds too, then has `packages` (the step, the packages, how long so far, the last line of the package log) and a `message` saying what to do.

include_code.description: Send the code even when it is unchanged since this session last read or wrote it. Default: false.

name: read_cell

description: See a cell's output as an image (PNG). Use it to check what a plot or figure looks like; `read_cell` only describes images. The call waits while cells run. It also works for an HTML output (a widget, an interactive plot) whose value has an image form or whose HTML holds the picture. In the Endeavor app on a Mac, while a Pluto notebook's pane is on screen, other HTML and WebGL outputs come back as the notebook draws them (`source: "screenshot"`). `read_cell` points to this tool when the HTML holds a picture; for other HTML it is worth a try. In safe preview it works only for an output that is already an image or HTML that holds one. Fails with `no_image` when the output has no image form (text, Markdown, and other HTML unless the Mac app took a picture of it): use `read_cell` for those.
name: view_cell_output

description: Replace a cell's code. The cell must have been read (`read_cell` or `read_notebook_code`) since it last changed, or the call fails with `read_required` or `stale_read`. The edit is staged, not run, unless `run_after` is true: `submit_changes` runs staged cells.

folded.description: Also hide (true) or show (false) the cell's code, as `fold_cell` does. Default: left as it is.

run_after.description: Run the cell right after the edit, without waiting for it. Default: false.

name: edit_cell

description: Replace the code of several cells in one call. Each must have been read first; if one has not, no cell is changed. Never runs them: `submit_changes` does. The receipt's `mutation.code_folded` says whether each cell's code is hidden after the edits.

cells.description: The edits, as {cell_id, code} objects, each with an optional `folded`.

folded.description: Also hide (true) or show (false) this cell's code, as `fold_cell` does. Default: left as it is.

name: edit_cells

description: Add a cell after `after_cell_id`, which must have been read first; leave it out only in an empty notebook. The new cell is staged, not run, and counts as read. Returns its `cell_id`.

code.description: The cell's code. Default: an empty cell.

folded.description: Hide the cell's code and show only its output. Use it for prose cells. Default: false.

run_after.description: Run the cell right after adding it, without waiting for it. Default: false.

name: add_cell

description: Delete a cell. Cells that depend on it run again, so this runs notebook code, and it can't be undone.
name: delete_cell

description: Run one cell and the cells that depend on it, whether or not it was edited. After edits, use `submit_changes` instead. Returns at once unless `wait_for_completion` is true, which waits at most 45 seconds; read the cell for its result.

wait_for_completion.description: Wait for the run to end, at most 45 seconds from the start of the call (at least 5 after an approval). If it is still going then, the result has the cells in `execution.still_running` (`status` is `running`, or `errored` if a cell already failed) and a `message`; the run continues, so read the cells later and do not run them again. Default: false.

name: execute_cell

description: Run the cells staged by edits (`pending_run`) and the cells that depend on them. Call it once after a batch of edits. Returns at once unless `wait_for_completion` is true, which waits at most 45 seconds; read the cells for their results. In safe preview nothing runs and the result warns `execution_blocked`.

cell_ids.description: Run only these staged cells. Default: every staged cell.

force.description: Allow `cell_ids` that are not staged. Default: false.

wait_for_completion.description: Wait for the run to end, at most 45 seconds from the start of the call (at least 5 after an approval). If it is still going then, the result has the cells in `execution.still_running` (`status` is `running`, or `errored` if a cell already failed) and a `message`; the run continues, so read the cells later and do not run them again. Default: false.

name: submit_changes

description: Run every cell in the notebook again, in dependency order. This can take long in a large notebook: after edits, `submit_changes` runs only what changed.

wait_for_completion.description: Wait for the run to end, at most 45 seconds from the start of the call (at least 5 after an approval). If it is still going then, the result has the cells in `execution.still_running` (`status` is `running`, or `errored` if a cell already failed) and a `message`; the run continues, so read the cells later and do not run them again. Default: false.

name: run_all_cells

description: Move a cell to just after another one. This changes the order on the page only; nothing runs.

after_cell_id.description: The cell to move after; "" moves it to the top.

name: move_cell

description: Fold or unfold a cell. A folded cell shows only its output, with its code hidden; use it for prose cells. Display only: nothing runs. Saved in the notebook file.

folded.description: true hides the code, false shows it.

name: fold_cell

description: Read the whole notebook as one string, each cell under a marker line with its id: `# ╔═╡ <id>` in a Pluto notebook, `# %% id=<id>` in an Ember one, as in the notebook's file. Counts as a read of every cell it returns. Markdown (prose) cells are left out unless `include_markdown` is true, so `cell_ids` can have fewer ids than the notebook has cells (`get_cell_order` lists all of them); when any are left out, `markdown_cells_left_out` says how many. The engine's own package cells are always left out.

include_markdown.description: Markdown cells are left out unless this is true; then each is included, marked `# md:` in a Pluto notebook (an Ember notebook's text cells are `#'` lines already). Default: false.

order.description: `execution` (the default): the order the cells run in. `visual`: their order on the page.

name: read_notebook_code

description: Return the cell ids in page order.
name: get_cell_order

description: Return the cell ids in the order the cells run.
name: get_execution_order

description: Return the cells a cell depends on (`upstream`) and the names it uses (`symbols`).
name: get_cell_dependencies

description: Return the cells that run again when this cell changes, directly or through other cells (`downstream`).
name: get_cell_dependents

description: Find the cells that define a name.
name: find_symbol_definitions

description: Find the cells that use a name, from analysis of the code; `search_code` matches text instead.
name: find_symbol_references

description: Check proposed code for a cell against the engine's parse rules, without changing the notebook. Returns `valid` and `errors`. It does not check names other cells define: use `find_symbol_definitions` for that.

cell_id.description: The cell the code is for.

name: validate_cell

description: Search the text of every cell's code, comments and strings included. Returns the matching cells, each with a snippet.
name: search_code

description: Keep a notebook running while it is idle. Otherwise a notebook stops after a stretch with no tool calls, edits or running cells (the user sets how long). Call it only when the user asks.

keep.description: true keeps it running until this is set back to false or the notebook is stopped.

name: keep_notebook_alive

description: Return whether the runtime is running and which notebooks are open. When the runtime is on a server or cluster, also what state it is in there. Use it when a notebook tool says the runtime isn't ready.
name: session_status

description: Open an existing notebook file the user named, and make it this session's notebook. When the user asks to open, show or look at a `.jl` or `.R` file, try it before reading the file; it fails with `not_a_notebook` if the file isn't one. It opens in safe preview: no code runs until the user allows it. If the file is already open, the session joins that notebook as it is (`already_open`) and nothing runs. Fails with `one_notebook` if the session already works in another notebook that is open.

path.description: The notebook file; a relative path is inside the session's folder.

run_notebook.description: Run the whole notebook once after opening, without waiting. Set it only when the user asked to run it. Default: false.

name: open_notebook

description: Create an empty notebook and make it this session's notebook, ready to run. Use it instead of writing a notebook file yourself: the runtime owns the file. It starts with one empty cell, whose id is in `cell_ids`: edit that cell first. Never overwrites a file. Fails with `one_notebook` if the session already works in a notebook that is open.

path.description: Where to create it, ending in `.jl` for a Julia notebook or `.R` for an R notebook (not on Windows); a relative path is inside the session's folder. The file must not exist yet and its folder must. Default: a notebook with a generated name in the session's folder, in R if the session was started for R notebooks and in Julia otherwise.

name: new_notebook

description: Take a notebook out of safe preview so that its code can run, as the user can from the notebook itself. Call it only when the user asked you to run the notebook: its code may not be theirs. By default it then runs the whole notebook once, without waiting.

run_notebook.description: false leaves safe preview without running anything; a later run also runs the cells it needs that never ran. Default: true.

name: allow_execution

description: Stop the notebook's run, as the Stop button in the notebook does: the running cells end interrupted and the queued ones don't run. It stops the whole run, whoever started it. Use it when the user asks you to stop, or for a run you started that is taking too long or is wrong. The result lists the cells that `stopped`, the queued cells `dropped`, and any `still_running`.
name: interrupt_notebook

description: Restart the notebook's process, as the Restart on the notebook's page does: every value is gone. A Julia notebook then runs every cell in the new process, including a cell that was stuck (named in `running_again`): edit such a cell first so it finishes. Read a cell to wait for the run. An R notebook's cells are left `not_run` until you run them (`run_all_cells` runs it from the top). Use it when the user asks for a fresh start, or, with the user's say-so, for an R cell that `interrupt_notebook` couldn't stop. Refused in safe preview.
name: restart_notebook

description: R notebooks only. An R notebook's package versions are those current on its package date (`package_date` in `list_notebooks` and `open_notebook`), so `available.packages()` in a cell lists that date's versions, not today's. This previews moving that date and changes nothing: the result has `changes` (each package's `from` and `to` versions) and any `problems`. Without `date` it previews today, which is what updating the packages means. It can take a while to fetch the date's package index; if `status` is still `fetching`, call it again with the same date.

date.description: A day as YYYY-MM-DD. Leave it out to update to today's packages.

name: preview_package_update

description: R notebooks only. Move the notebook's package date to the `date` of a `preview_package_update` whose `status` is `ready`, applying exactly the `changes` it showed. Refused with `no_preview` if there is no such preview, or the notebook's packages changed since. The file's date and package versions change, the new library installs, and if R had a changed package loaded it restarts and every cell is left `not_run`. Use it when the user asked to update the packages or move the date, after telling them what changes.
name: apply_package_update

description: R notebooks only. Say yes to a large download: an install whose Bioconductor annotation and experiment-data packages add up to more than 500 MB (Ember's default limit) stops before downloading anything, and its cells wait, queued, with `packages.step` `asking` and `packages.download` listing the packages and their sizes. Call it only after the user said yes to that download; never on your own. Refused with `nothing_to_approve` when no install is waiting for an OK, or the notebook isn't allowed to run yet. The library then installs and the queued cells run.
name: approve_install
